subject: Risk & Compliance
title: What Makes White-Collar Crime Different
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Makes White-Collar Crime Different usable.

hook.text: A bank robber gets 20 years. A CEO who steals a hundred times more gets probation. Same crime, different collar.

buildup.text: White-collar crime is nonviolent, financially motivated crime committed by business professionals in positions of trust.

discovery.text: The term was coined in 1939 by sociologist Edwin Sutherland, who argued the rich commit crime too.

twist.text: White-collar criminals exploit trust and access. The damage is often larger but less visible than street crime.

climax.text: A single white-collar scheme can destroy more wealth than every bank robbery in the country combined.

punchline.text: No gun needed. Just trust, access, and a spreadsheet.
